result.title: High-dimensional layer-state trajectories reveal the internal dynamics of transformer inference
result.comment: Expanded preprint with 17 main figures and 13 supplementary figures. Source data and code are archived on Zenodo
result.summary: Mechanistic studies of large language models localize function in parameters, attention heads or neurons, but those parts do not specify how one inference unfolds. We treat the ordered layer-state trajectory as the empirical process and test whether layer order defines a measurable computation. Across representative Qwen, Llama and Gemma checkpoints, realized order produced paths 1.60--2.24 times as aligned with their endpoint chord as endpoint-preserving shuffles. The order effect transferred to a lexical task, but was stronger in three random initializations of the same Qwen architecture, identifying an architecture-compatible scaffold rather than a training-specific law. Direct hidden states provided stronger mechanism coordinates than vocabulary readbacks, and a task-defined coordinate made candidate competition computable. After additive interventions failed, local transition actuators selectively controlled internal trajectories across checkpoints. A confidence gate then drove 17 of 87 held-out Qwen closure trajectories across the full-vocabulary top-1 candidate boundary while leaving all 203 non-closure top-1 outputs unchanged. Safety-matched action reassignment performed similarly, locating the gain in selective gating and the bounded actuator family rather than fine-grained dose assignment. Layer order exposes an observable, computable and behaviourally consequential process of transformer inference without establishing a complete theory of LLM dynamics or control of answer correctness.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把 Transformer 推理刻画为按层序展开的隐状态轨迹，通过对比真实层序与保持端点的层序打乱来量化层序的计算效应，并用局部转移执行器与置信门控检验该轨迹过程是否可计算、可干预且有行为后果。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽不含视觉或多模态推理，但其把层间隐状态轨迹当作可测量过程、以打乱层序作对照、并用执行器与置信门控选择性改变内部轨迹的做法，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 轨迹几何、状态更新与停止门控的分析与因果证据设计。
